newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN rights envoy in Cambodia condemns coup d'etat.
newsitem.headline: UN rights envoy in Cambodia condemns coup d'etat.

text.p: The U.N. secretary general's special envoy on human rights in Cambodia on Tuesday condemned the coup d'etat there and called for parliamentarians and opposition politicians to be protected.
Envoy Thomas Hammarberg expressed concern at the large loss of life in the current violence and the atmosphere of fear prevailing in Cambodia.

"I strongly condemn the violent coup d'etat of 5-6 July which has displaced the lawfully elected government of Cambodia," the Swedish diplomat said in a statement issued by the United Nations in Geneva.
"I call on the de facto authorities to reverse this illegal action," he added.
Second Prime Minister Hun Sen toppled First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh, head of the FUNCINPEC party, after fighting between factional troops at the weekend.
Their two-headed coalition government was formed after a United Nations-run election in 1993.
Amnesty International on Tuesday accused Cambodian forces loyal to Hun Sen of conducting a violent campaign of intimidation, arrests and harassment of politicians, party activists and journalists.
More than 50 people were said to be in hiding or in need of protection in the southeast Asian nation.
Hammarberg said Ranariddh must be allowed to reassume his office and no member of the National Assembly should be expelled because they hold different political views.

"The safety of all members of the National Assembly, members of opposition political parties, human rights workers and journalists must be protected," he added. "No person should be arrested because of their political views."

Anyone arrested or detained must be fully accounted for and held only in legally-established places of detention, according to the envoy. He said the United Nations and International Committee of the Red Cross should have access to all areas.
